name: METAL GEAR SOLID V: THE PHANTOM PAIN

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh and 40 fps lock gives buttery-smooth, tear-free gameplay with a good visual balance. High textures keep the cinematic Fox Engine presentation intact while medium shadows and FSR upscaling keep the GPU load in check.

profiles.Summary: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain runs well on the Steam Deck under Proton, with a platinum ProtonDB rating and strong community confidence. The Fox Engine is relatively well-optimised and the game's PC requirements are modest enough that the Deck can handle it comfortably at medium-to-high settings targeting 40–60 fps.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck tuning reports were available; profiles are estimated from the platinum ProtonDB tier, the game's modest PC requirements (GTX 650 minimum / GTX 760 recommended), and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capability. On your first run, check frame pacing in a large open-world area and drop to the Optimal profile if you see sustained dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping to a sub-native render resolution with FSR upscaling and a 7 W TDP cap squeezes maximum battery life while keeping the game playable. The Fox Engine holds 30 fps comfortably at these settings even in open-world areas.

KnownIssues: Occasional stuttering during large open-world traversal or busy combat sequences
Some users report needing to verify game files or tweak Proton version if the game fails to launch
Online/FOB multiplayer features may be unreliable or non-functional under Proton
In-app purchase / microtransaction menus may not function correctly

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Fox Engine is well-optimised and the Deck can sustain near-60 fps at native 1280x800 with high settings in most scenarios; expect occasional dips to 50 fps in densely packed outdoor areas. Battery drain will be high, so keep a charger handy.

Optimal.Notes: At 1152x720 with medium-high settings the Fox Engine runs very comfortably on the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, holding close to 60 fps in most open-world areas; FSR at sharpness 3 upscales cleanly to 1280x800. Motion blur is disabled as it adds little at 60 fps and costs GPU time.

profiles.Summary: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain runs well on the Steam Deck, benefiting from its age (2015) and relatively modest PC requirements that the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds. ProtonDB reports a platinum rating with strong confidence, meaning it is largely plug-and-play with Proton, though the Playable Deck Verified status hints at minor UI or input quirks.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest 2015 PC requirements (GTX 650 minimum, GTX 760 recommended), the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class), and the strong platinum ProtonDB rating. On your first run, check frame rate during open-world exploration — if the Optimal profile dips below 50 fps in busy areas, lower Shadow Quality to Low and reduce LOD one step.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping to 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a 7 W TDP cap keeps the battery going well over four hours while the 30 fps lock remains stable throughout. FSR sharpness 4 recovers most of the visual clarity lost from the lower render resolution.

KnownIssues: Steam Deck Verified status is 'Playable' rather than 'Verified', suggesting some interface elements or text may be small or not fully optimized for the screen
Online/FOB multiplayer features may have connectivity or compatibility issues under Proton
In-App Purchases and some online menus may be awkward to navigate with controller
Occasional stutters reported during open-world traversal in dense areas, though generally minor

MaxPerformance.Notes: MGSV's 2015 Fox Engine is light enough that the Deck can push native 1280x800 at high settings and reach the 90 Hz ceiling in most scenes; expect occasional dips to the 65-75 range in the densest open-world areas. Battery life will be short at full TDP, so keep a charger handy.
